decisions.reason: As a multi-model underground dump truck line tied to the firm's publicly stated underground equipment strategy, management is inclined to continue despite mixed evidence and can still interpret weak results as cyclical mining or recent market disruptions rather than a definitive failure.

The construction site dumper is a more limited commitment than a broad product family, so withdrawal is more conceivable, but after several years on offer management would still resist admitting failure and can blame any underperformance on temporary construction, supply, and ramp-up issues.

This multi-model inclined furniture lift line fits the firm's lifting and service capabilities, and the visible standalone presentation creates enough sunk-cost and reputational pressure for management to persist.

The inclined building material lift line is close to the firm's core lifting applications and was publicly committed as its own range, so escalation of commitment makes continued support more likely than withdrawal.

The truck-mounted inclined furniture lift is a narrower variant and therefore somewhat easier to cut than the broader lift lines, but its connection to the same platform and service logic still pushes management toward retention.
